## TEAM USA

Competitions

### INTERCONTINENTAL

JANSEN

CUP

## The Jansen Cup is the premier international FootGolf competition, inspired by the storied tradition of the Ryder Cup in golf. This biennial event brings together the finest FootGolf players from Great Britain and North America in a battle for national pride. The Jansen Cup honors the legacy of Michael Jansen, a pioneer in FootGolf's development. The inaugural Jansen Cup was held ninety years after the first Ryder Cup, marking a new era in FootGolf's history. The European team, comprising talented players from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales, faced off against Team USA in a thrilling display of skill and sportsmanship. This groundbreaking event was made possible by the vision and dedication of Laura and Roberto Balestrini.  
  
 The next edition, 100 years after the launch of the Ryder Cup, will feature a team from Canada, Mexico, and the United States versus a team formed by players from England, Scotland, and Wales, celebrating the 10th Anniversary of the event. Join us on this journey as we honor the past, celebrate the present, and shape the future of FootGolf.

![Image 11: jansen_cup_logo_color_space.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_f506aceb9b4a4d6bb91a67396c3f66c8~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_264,h_243,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/jansen_cup_logo_color_space.png)

### INTERNATIONAL

BATTLE OF

THE BORDER

## The Battle of the Border is a prestigious international FootGolf tournament, conceived by the FootGolf Federations of the United States and Mexico to commemorate the enduring partnership between the two organizations. This multi-day, multicategory event unites the National FootGolf Teams from both nations, showcasing their exceptional skills and reinforcing the strong bond between them – one of the most storied and resilient relationships in the global FootGolf community.  
  
 The inaugural Battle of the Border took place in 2019 in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico, setting the stage for a thrilling rivalry. Later that year, the second installment of the tournament was held in Palm Springs, California, featuring an electrifying match between the two teams. In 2024, the third edition of the tournament brought the teams together once again at the Chimera Golf Club in Las Vegas, Nevada.

![Image 12: BOB_logo_color_space.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_726543aefadd4ec5949631e511237346~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_264,h_243,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/BOB_logo_color_space.png)

### INTERCONTINENTAL

FIFG WORLD CHAMPIONS CUP

## The FIFG World Champions Cup is the pinnacle of international FootGolf competition, featuring FIFG Member Countries that have previously won the FIFG World Cup National Team category. Organized by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG), this event brings together the world's top FootGolf nations to compete for the coveted "World Champions Cup" title. As new teams win the World Cup, they earn a spot in this exclusive competition, fostering a dynamic and ever-changing field of competitors. The United States National FootGolf Team, represented by the American FootGolf Federation, earned a spot in the inaugural edition of the FIFG World Champions Cup after winning the FIFG World Cup Argentina 2016 in the Men's category.  
  
 USA FootGolf is proud to represent the United States in this competition. The location and date of the tournament will be determined Competitions Committee of the Federation for International FootGolf. We look forward to announcing the details and cheering on Team USA as they compete for the World Champions Cup title.

![Image 13: world_champions_cup_space.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_5dfdc19929b94823be9bb0c440f94f05~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_264,h_243,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/world_champions_cup_space.png)

### INTERCONTINENTAL

PACIFIC

TROPHY

## The Pacific Trophy is an intercontinental FootGolf competition, created by The Balestrinis (United States) and Shinpei Matsuura (Japan). This biennial event brings together the finest FootGolf players from participating countries, celebrating the pioneers of FootGolf's development. The inaugural Pacific Trophy took place in 2016 at the AFGL Home Course in the California Desert, featuring a thrilling match between Team Japan and Team USA, and marking a significant milestone in FootGolf's history.

# U.S. Governing Body

### AMERICAN FOOTGOLF FEDERATION

American FootGolf Federation is the governing body and exclusive member of the Federation for International FootGolf in the United States.

FootGolf as a game has been played around the world since forever but, as a sport it is regulated by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) since July, 2012.The FIFG created the FootGolf Rulebook in 2013. The New Rulebook was approved and used for the first time in December 2018, during the FIFG FootGolf World Cup in Marrakesh, Morocco.

​

" Mankind's evolution is visible in many ways and the first decade of the new millennium brought us 'The Best Game Ever Invented'. A game that upgraded the world of sports to a new dimension, combining the power, elegance and precision of the number one elite sport in the world: GOLF, with the passion, energy and fun of the most popular sport in the world: SOCCER, in a marvelous sport full of life: FOOTGOLF, THE SPORT YOU ARE GOING TO PLAY!"

​

​

LAURA BALESTRINI

Co-Founder & President • United States FootGolf

![Image 3: 8C9A0008.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_3f4ab71db3f242578ce2b43ac9911e8e~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_590,h_340,fp_0.48_0.85,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/8C9A0008.jpg)

### OUR MISSION  
To promote and govern the sport of FootGolf throughout the United States.

OUR VISION

Grow the sport of FootGolf from its base, focusing on the youth, recreational and amateur aspects of the sport while making FootGolf a massive and popular sport that is accessible to all.

![Image 4: 8C9A0161.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_314df1356b8b4c648bd21e2fe259523a~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_590,h_340,fp_0.49_0.60,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/8C9A0161.jpg)

![Image 5: AFGF_web_2025_back_red.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_711418f55cd14b1c89bdb867fa317c24~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_1280,h_488,fp_0.29_0.92,q_90,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/ef005a_711418f55cd14b1c89bdb867fa317c24~mv2.png)

## FootGolf Needs Your Support Today!

[Donate](link_22)

[Volunteer](link_1)

## AMERICAN FOOTGOLF FEDERATION

Sport Development

As the sport of FootGolf continues to grow the need for Sport Development is becoming a key focus in keeping our athletes mentally and physically strong. As we discover current players and new partners who have athletic training as either coaches, physical therapists, trainers or who have played other sports professionally we will tap into their knowledge to build our development programs.Since the goal of the Federation for International FootGolf is to become a full member of the Sports Accord therein paving our path to someday being an Olympic sport, we want to prepare our players to compete at a high level. Some of the ways that we will prepare our players at all levels is through sport development programs.

![Image 6: AFGF_web_2025_sport_development.jpg](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_d718901fd126477e8f292e910352eddd~mv2.jpg/v1/fill/w_551,h_380,fp_0.45_0.37,q_80,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/AFGF_web_2025_sport_development.jpg)

### Community Clinics and Training Camps

Encouraging young athletes to participate and learn FootGolf skills with activities that enhance balance, coordination, cardiovascular fitness and focus.

Focus on Player Development

This includes both technical and non-technical skills, such as mental resilience and concentration, which are crucial for success on the course.

### Physical Training

A well-structured strength and conditioning program can positively impact footgolfers performance, increasing kicking distance and reducing injury risk.

![Image 7: AFGF_web_2025_back.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_2193f91a5a254854b4f3af2085bb4e30~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_1280,h_390,al_c,q_90,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/ef005a_2193f91a5a254854b4f3af2085bb4e30~mv2.png)

## These programs will emphasize a holistic approach, balancing talent development with the athlete's well-being and long-term success.

Youth FootGolf

The American FootGolf Federation is in the beginning stages of developing Youth programs and initiatives that introduce the game to youth through schools, park and recreation programs and organizations that service at-risk kids in our communities, The focus will be on giving kids a physical and mental outlet, allowing children to focus on the activity and skill development, and foster character and life skills.These programs aim to make FootGolf accessible, fun, and inclusive, while also building our future of the sport.

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

World's governing body for the footgolf

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/4/46/Robot_Not.svg/60px-Robot_Not.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robot_Not.svg "link")This article **incorporates text from a [large language model](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Large_language_models "Wikipedia:Large language models"), which is [prohibited in Wikipedia articles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:LLM "Wikipedia:LLM")**. It may include [hallucinated](link_3) information, [copyright violations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:COPYVIO "Wikipedia:COPYVIO"), claims not [verified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:V "Wikipedia:V") in cited sources, [original research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:OR "Wikipedia:OR"), or [fictitious references](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Fictitious_references "Wikipedia:Fictitious references"). Any such material should be [removed](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federation_for_International_FootGolf&action=edit)._(September 2026)_ _([Learn how and when to remove this message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Maintenance\_template\_removal "Help:Maintenance template removal"))_

Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) has been advancing and developing [FootGolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footgolf "Footgolf") as a standardised global sport since 2012. Headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, FIFG promotes the global recognition and development of FootGolf, establishes and enforces standardised international rules, organises major competitions (including the FIFG World Cup, FIFG World Tour and FIFG Regional Tours), and regulates national member associations.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federation_for_International_FootGolf&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

**Origins and early variants**

For decades, games conceptually similar to FootGolf were played informally across the globe on beaches, farms, parks, and other open spaces. These informal variants emerged under a variety of local names, including [Codeball](link_4), Footballgolf, foot-golf, Futgolf, Soccer-Golf, Kick-golf, Footee, and [Buschball](link_5) and operated under localised rules that often differed significantly from one another.

The modern standardised format of the game emerged in the Netherlands between 2008 and 2010 when Michael Jansen and Bas Korsten developed a rule set based on traditional golf. They subsequently organised the world’s first official tournament on a regulation golf course, establishing the foundational template that would later be adopted globally.

**The International FootGolf Association and structural challenges**

Although Michael Jansen and his business partners intended to lay the initial foundations for international governance by creating the International FootGolf Association (IFGA) during the 2009-2010 period, the transition from a localised concept into a structured international sport proved exceptionally difficult. Due to the overwhelming financial burdens of global distances and restrictive economics, the IFGA went dormant. To end confusion and potential organisational rivalries and unite the sport under a single banner, the IFGA officially recognised the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) as the sole global governing body for the sport. The FIFG recognised Michael Jansen as a co‑creator of the basic modern rules of the sport as it is played today and serves the organisation as an FIFG Ambassador and Honorary Board Member. [CNN](link_6)

**Foundation and growth of the FIFG**

The Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) was formally established in 2012 by sports enthusiasts who united their resources to create a unified global governing body. The federation was publicly announced in June 2012 during the inaugural FootGolf World Cup held near Budapest, Hungary. Today the FIFG maintains its international headquarters at Place Saint‑François 7, 1003 Lausanne, Switzerland. While casual FootGolf is estimated to be played in over one hundred countries, the regulated competitive sport is strictly organised by multiple member countries under the FIFG framework.

**Founding**

The FIFG was founded by Roberto Balestrini, Laura Balestrini, and Francisco Gonzalez Briones from FIFG Region 1 – North America; Javier de Ancizar from FIFG Region 2 – South America; and Gábor Gelencser, Mauritz van Tubergen, and Leonardo Decaria from FIFG Region 3 – Europe. Working together to establish the FIFG as the sport’s international governing body, they coordinated with Hungary's Gábor Gelencser to host the first FIFG FootGolf World Cup near Budapest in June 2012, which featured 126 excited players from eight countries.

## Name and branding

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federation_for_International_FootGolf&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Name and branding")]

The Federation for International FootGolf adopted and standardised the sport’s name under it's brand as a single word with a capital F and a capital G: FootGolf. Accordingly, the sport governed by FIFG rules and guidelines is officially identified as FootGolf, and the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) promotes the sport under this trademarked title, having published and periodically updated an official rulebook since 2012 to ensure uniform rules worldwide.

## Structure and leadership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federation_for_International_FootGolf&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Structure and leadership")]

FIFG is governed by a Board of Directors, which functions as the central decision-making body responsible for strategic direction, policy development, and oversight of the sport’s global administration. The board approves key initiatives, including rules and policies, through convened meetings where members deliberate on matters such as competition structures, membership criteria, and organisational reforms.

The board comprises defined leadership roles: President – leads overall operations and represents FIFG internationally 1st Vice President and 2nd Vice President – assist in executive duties and chair specific initiatives General Secretary – manages administrative affairs, including correspondence and record-keeping Treasurer – oversees financial matters Additional board members and advisors

Past presidents: Javier de Ancizar, Mauritz van Tubergen, Michael O'Connor, Roberto Balestrini, Gabor Gelencser, Laura Balestrini. Current president: Aleksander Kravanja

On October 3, 2017, the [Global Association of International Sports Federations](link_7) announced the federation as one of the first international federations to achieve Observer status.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-3)

That year also saw the introduction of FIFG Regional Majors and ranked tournaments, such as the FIFG 500 series, to promote sustained player development and event diversity across continents.

## Core responsibilities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federation_for_International_FootGolf&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Core responsibilities")]

Rule Standardisation: Establishes and maintains the Official FIFG Rulebook, guidelines, and player codes of conduct to guarantee consistent gameplay worldwide.

Global Tournaments: Organises the premier international competitions for the sport, including the official FootGolf Tours and the multi-category FootGolf World Cup.

National Affiliation: Dictates membership frameworks, recognising only one exclusive national organisation per country to govern local play.

Dispute Resolution: Exercises sole jurisdiction over resolving institutional conflicts or administrative disagreements between member countries or continental federations.

Sport Integrity & Anti-Doping: Protects the integrity of the sport by mandating strict ethical guidelines, combating corruption, and delivering anti-doping programmes in partnership with the International Testing Agency] ([ITA](link_8)).

Inclusivity & Growth: Sets mandatory criteria for its member nations to expand the sport at the grassroots level, specifically promoting the inclusion of women, youth, and athletes with disabilities.

References

*   Organises official FootGolf Tours[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-5)
*   Organises the Footgolf World Cup[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-8)
*   Regulates [member](link_9) countries[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-9)
*   Sets the [rules](link_10) of the sport [[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federation_for_International_FootGolf#cite_note-10)

## Members

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Federation_for_International_FootGolf&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Members")]

The Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) recognises only one exclusive member per [country](link_9). Membership is restricted to a single national organisation that serves as the official governing body for the sport within its territory. Players are required to affiliate with the FIFG member organisation of their country of birth or permanent residence. Unrepresented countries may apply to initiate the formal membership process. To achieve official recognition, an applicant national organisation must satisfy requirements across four primary categories: governance, universality, ethics, and responsibility.

**Governance**

. Institutional Structure: The applicant must be a legally registered national organisation governed by a general assembly as its supreme decision‑making body.

. Administrative Principles: Organizations must implement principles of good governance, including transparency, accountability, gender equity, non‑discrimination, and institutional fairness.

**Universality and Development**

. Domestic Competition: The organisation must actively develop the sport by hosting a minimum of three tournaments annually, distributed across at least two distinct golf courses.

. International Integration: Scheduled events must attract a significant field of competitive players who are formally affiliated with existing FIFG member countries.

**Ethics and Responsibility**

. Inclusivity and Safety: Member organisations must promote inclusive participation—specifically for women and individuals with disabilities, while supporting "sport for all" initiatives. They are required to uphold high-standard officiating, clear competition rules, fair play, and athlete health and safety protocols.

. Anti-Doping Compliance: The organisation must be a signatory to the World Anti‑Doping Code, maintain domestic anti‑doping regulations aligned with the Code, and actively participate in anti-doping initiatives.

. Integrity Safeguards: Organisations must implement formal frameworks to protect athletes and sports personnel from corruption, fraudulent activities, illegal or irregular sports betting, and other malicious practices.

# Is FootGolf a Real Sport? Here's the Proof

Published February 10, 2026· Updated July 18, 2026

It's a fair question. On paper, FootGolf sounds like something invented on a slow afternoon: kick a soccer ball around a golf course. But look past the novelty and you'll find every hallmark of a legitimate, organized sport.

## It has an official governing body

FootGolf is organized internationally by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG), which sets standardized rules, sanctions courses, and runs the FootGolf World Cup between national teams. In the United States, the American FootGolf League (AFGL) plays the equivalent role: approving courses, running a season-long tour, and enforcing a formal player code of conduct.

## It has competitive infrastructure

Real sports have standings, sanctioned venues, and a path from casual play to competition. FootGolf checks every box: AFGL-affiliated courses must meet specific equipment and layout standards, tour stops carry ranking points, and top finishers can qualify to represent their country at international events.

## It rewards genuine skill

Ask anyone who's played 18 holes of FootGolf: distance control with your feet is a real, learnable skill, not a novelty. Reading the break on a 40-foot approach kick, choosing the right strike (laces vs. inside-of-foot), and managing wind on a long par 5 all separate good players from great ones, the same skill gap that exists in traditional golf.

## So why does it still feel casual?

Because it's accessible. You don't need years of coaching or expensive clubs to enjoy a round, which makes FootGolf feel more like a fun outing than golf sometimes does. That accessibility is a feature, not evidence that the sport isn't "real": plenty of legitimate sports (pickleball, disc golf) share the same low barrier to entry alongside a genuine competitive scene.

Curious how a round actually works? Our [full guide](https://footgolfsport.com/how-to-play-footgolf) covers rules, scoring, and etiquette for your first 18.

## Frequently asked questions

Is FootGolf a real sport?Yes. FootGolf has an international governing body (the Federation for International FootGolf), national federations in dozens of countries, a FIFG World Cup between national teams, and a professional-style tour structure in the US through the American FootGolf League.

Is FootGolf hard?FootGolf is easy to pick up but hard to master. Basic contact is simple for most players, but consistent accuracy over 18 holes, reading greens, and controlling distance with your feet takes real practice.

# The FootGolf World Cup: Editions, Hosts and Champions

Published September 27, 2026

The FootGolf World Cup is the sport's flagship event, run by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG). It is not an annual tournament: according to FIFG's [champions list](https://footgolf.sport/champions/), it has been held in 2012, 2016, 2018, 2023 and 2026. The most recent edition was played in Acapulco, Mexico, in mid-2026.

## Every edition and its individual champions

*   2012, Budapest, Hungary: the first World Cup. Men's individual champion: Bela Lengyel (Hungary)
*   2016, Argentina: men's individual champion Christian Otero (Argentina)
*   2018, Marrakech, Morocco: men's champion Matias Perrone (Argentina); women's champion Sophie Brown (England); senior champion Stefano Grigolo (Italy)
*   2023, Orlando, USA: men's champion Bence Bacskai (Hungary); women's champion Lucia Cermakova (Slovakia); senior champion Jan Aksel Odden (Norway)
*   2026, Acapulco, Mexico: men's champion Florian Warsemann (France); women's champion Lucia Cermakova (Slovakia); senior champion Christian Fernandez (Argentina); senior plus champion Sergio Toth (Argentina)

Sophie Brown's 2018 win is recorded by Guinness World Records as the [first women's World Cup title](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/567869-first-fifg-footgolf-world-cup-winner-female). Team titles are decided separately from the individual ones.

## Team champions

*   2016: USA
*   2018: France
*   2023: France (men), Argentina (senior men), Japan (women)
*   2026: France (men), Argentina (senior men), France (women)

These come from FIFG's [champions list](https://footgolf.sport/champions/) and the [Orlando 2023 recap](https://www.orlando2023.com/post/the-fifg-footgolf-world-cup-orlando-2023-crowns-its-world-champions). We could not verify a team winner for 2012 or a senior plus team winner for 2026.

## How the 2026 event worked

The 2026 World Cup ran an individual championship from May 27 to June 1 and a team championship from June 2 to 7, on two courses, Turtle Dunes Country Club and Tres Vidas Golf Club. Categories were men, senior men and senior plus for individuals, plus a women's competition. FIFG's [report on the individual results](https://www.footgolf.sport/acapulcoworldcup2026/acapulco-2026-crowns-its-individual-world-champions/) says the men's title went to a playoff, and that England's Ben Clarke shot a 60 in the final round.

FIFG's own pages give different headcounts for the field, so we won't quote one; it drew hundreds of players from more than 50 nations.

## Is there a next one?

FIFG's champions list shows no World Cup between 2018 and 2023, and as of late September 2026 we could not find an announced host or date for the next edition. FIFG's site is the place to watch for it. It is currently promoting a Youth World Cup in Germany in 2026.

New to the governing bodies? Our [What Is FootGolf](https://footgolfsport.com/what-is-footgolf) guide explains FIFG's role, and [the American FootGolf League explained](https://footgolfsport.com/blog/american-footgolf-league-explained) covers the US side. Wondering whether there is money in the competitive game? See [how much FootGolf players make](https://footgolfsport.com/blog/how-much-do-footgolf-players-make).

# FootGolf: The Sport Where You Kick Your Way Around 18 Holes

FootGolf is real golf, played with your feet. Swap the clubs for a soccer ball, keep the same scorecard, and play one of the fastest-growing sports in the country, on courses you already know.

[Learn The Rules](https://footgolfsport.com/how-to-play-footgolf)[Find A Course Near Me](https://footgolfsport.com/find-footgolf-courses-near-me)

![Image 1: A player about to kick a soccer ball toward the green on a FootGolf hole](https://footgolfsport.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpicsum.photos%2Fseed%2Ffootgolfsport-hero-fairway%2F900%2F700&w=3840&q=75)

2008

Created in the Netherlands

18

Holes per round, same as golf

## What Is FootGolf?

FootGolf takes the layout, etiquette, and scoring of golf and swaps the clubs and small ball for a soccer ball and your feet. Players kick from a tee box toward a hole about 20 inches (50 to 52 cm) wide cut into the green, using the same par, bunkers, hazards, and 18-hole structure as traditional golf.

Organized FootGolf is widely credited to Bas Korsten and Michael Jansen, who created the sport in the Netherlands in 2008. The sport has since spread to dozens of countries and is now governed internationally by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG), with the American FootGolf League (AFGL)overseeing sanctioned courses and tournaments across the United States.

[Read the full history and explanation](https://footgolfsport.com/what-is-footgolf)

![Image 2: Close-up of a soccer ball resting beside an oversized FootGolf hole on the green](https://footgolfsport.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpicsum.photos%2Fseed%2Ffootgolfsport-oversized-hole%2F900%2F700&w=3840&q=75)

## Why People Are Falling For FootGolf

![Image 3: A group of friends walking the fairway during a FootGolf round](https://footgolfsport.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpicsum.photos%2Fseed%2Ffootgolfsport-group-round%2F900%2F700&w=1920&q=75)

Genuine Competition

Behind the casual vibe is a real competitive scene: sanctioned AFGL tour stops, national rankings, and a FIFG World Cup.

### Easy To Learn

If you can kick a ball, you can play. There's no swing to master, so it's approachable for total beginners and families alike.

### A Real Workout

An 18-hole round means miles of walking plus the balance and accuracy of a controlled kick, good cardio dressed up as a laid-back afternoon.

## How To Play FootGolf

FootGolf follows the same flow as a round of golf: play in groups set by the course (commonly up to four players), moving through the holes in order. Full rules, scoring, group etiquette, and technique tips for your first round are covered in our complete guide.

1.   1
Tee off

Start with the ball inside the tee zone at the tee markers.

2.   2
Play it as it lies

Keep kicking from wherever the ball stops, without improving your lie.

3.   3
Mind the flag

You can have the flagstick removed, but nobody may hold it while you kick.

4.   4
Hole out

The round ends when the ball drops into the cup; write down your score.

[See the full rules & scoring guide](https://footgolfsport.com/how-to-play-footgolf)

![Image 4: Turf shoes and an approved size 5 FootGolf ball laid out on the fairway](https://footgolfsport.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpicsum.photos%2Fseed%2Ffootgolfsport-shoes-ball%2F900%2F700&w=1920&q=75)

## What To Wear & Bring

Most FootGolf courses enforce the same dress code as their golf side: collared shirts, golf shorts or pants, and turf or indoor soccer shoes instead of cleats. Bring your own approved ball if you have one, a towel, and sunscreen for a full 18.

*   Collared shirt
*   Golf shorts, pants, or skirt
*   Turf or indoor soccer shoes
*   Approved size 5 FootGolf ball

[Full equipment & dress code guide](https://footgolfsport.com/footgolf-equipment-and-dress-code)

![Image 5: Aerial view of a golf course with a FootGolf layout marked across the fairways](https://footgolfsport.com/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpicsum.photos%2Fseed%2Ffootgolfsport-course-aerial%2F1400%2F600&w=3840&q=75)

## Find FootGolf Courses Near You

FootGolf courses now operate in nearly every US region, from dedicated facilities to traditional golf courses that added a FootGolf layout. We break down how to find a sanctioned course near you and how AFGL affiliation works.

[Start Your Course Search](https://footgolfsport.com/find-footgolf-courses-near-me)

## Common Questions

A few things almost everyone asks before their first round.

[Browse all FootGolf FAQs and articles](https://footgolfsport.com/blog)

What is FootGolf?FootGolf is a hybrid sport that combines soccer and golf. Players kick a soccer ball around a golf course and try to get it into an oversized hole in as few kicks as possible, using standard golf scoring (par, birdie, bogey, etc.).

Is FootGolf a real, organized sport?Yes. FootGolf is organized internationally by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG) and in the United States by the American FootGolf League (AFGL), which run sanctioned tournaments and maintain official rules.

Do I need special equipment to play FootGolf?You need a size 5 soccer ball approved for FootGolf play and comfortable athletic or turf shoes. Most courses provide or sell approved balls, so equipment costs to get started are minimal.

Get the full rulebook, find a course, and gear up. Everything you need to tee (kick) off starts here.

# How To Play FootGolf: Rules, Scoring & Etiquette

Everything you need to walk onto a FootGolf course for the first time and play a confident, correct round, from tee to cup.

## The core rules

1.   Start each hole with the ball inside the tee zone, the area behind the tee markers. It doesn't have to leave between the markers, but it must start inside the zone.
2.   Play the ball as it lies: you can't improve your position, stance, or line. A ball not found within three minutes is lost, and you can declare a ball unplayable and, with a penalty, drop it or return to where you last kicked.
3.   You can have the flagstick removed before you kick, but nobody may hold or attend it while you do. Put it back in the hole before you leave the green.
4.   The hole ends the moment the ball drops into the cup. Record your total number of kicks for that hole.
5.   The course or tournament sets the groups, commonly up to four players. Groups play the holes in order, and a slower group lets faster ones play through.
6.   Cleats of any kind are not allowed under FIFG rules: turf shoes or indoor soccer shoes protect the greens the way golf spikes do.

New to the course? Our[seven beginner tips](https://footgolfsport.com/blog/footgolf-tips-for-beginners)cover the rules first-timers most often get wrong.

## Watch: the official beginner tutorial

The American FootGolf League's tutorial, "New to FootGolf? Start here", covers the essential rules, techniques, and tips for first-timers.

[Video 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uTf9eyZLTDA)

## How scoring works

FootGolf scoring is identical to golf. Every hole has a par: the number of kicks an experienced player is expected to need. Your score relative to par uses the same familiar language:

*   **Eagle**: two under par
*   **Birdie**: one under par
*   **Par**: matching the hole's expected score
*   **Bogey**: one over par
*   **Double bogey**: two over par

Add up your score across all 18 holes to get your round total, exactly like a golf scorecard. Match play, penalties, and tie-breaks work differently: see our[FootGolf scoring guide](https://footgolfsport.com/blog/footgolf-scoring-explained).

## Kicking technique that actually helps

### Strike with your laces for distance

For tee shots and long approaches, striking through the laces gives you the most power and the straightest ball flight, the FootGolf equivalent of a full swing.

### Use the inside of your foot for touch

Around the green, a controlled push with the inside of your foot gives you far more accuracy than trying to blast it close: think of it as your putting stroke.

### Practice both feet

You'll inevitably face a lie that favors your weaker foot. Players who can kick competently with either foot avoid awkward, low-percentage shots off tricky lies.

### Read the wind before long kicks

A soccer ball is lighter and rounder than a golf ball, so wind affects it more over distance. Check the wind before committing to a long approach the same way a golfer checks it before a driver swing.

### Know the course before you play

Bunkers, water, and out-of-bounds all count in FootGolf exactly as they do in golf. A quick look at the course layout (many clubs post a FootGolf-specific map) helps you avoid an easily avoidable penalty stroke.

## Etiquette every beginner should know

*   Stay behind players who are about to kick, and stay quiet during their approach.
*   Repair any divots you take from the fairway.
*   Keep pace: if your group falls behind, let faster players play through.
*   Replace the flag carefully once your group has finished the hole.
*   Follow any course-specific dress code, covered in full in our equipment guide.

Not sure what to wear or bring? Check our[full equipment and dress code guide](https://footgolfsport.com/footgolf-equipment-and-dress-code)before you book a tee time.

## Frequently asked questions

What are the basic rules of FootGolf?Each hole starts with the ball inside the tee zone, players kick the ball from wherever it comes to rest, and the hole ends once the ball is kicked into the cup. Courses set the groups, commonly up to four players, and scoring follows standard golf par terminology.

How do you keep score in FootGolf?Exactly like golf: count every kick it takes to get the ball into the hole, then compare that number to the hole's par. A round total is the sum of strokes across all 18 (or 9) holes relative to total par.

Are cleats allowed in FootGolf?No. FIFG rules ban cleats of any kind, along with golf shoes, and most courses follow suit to protect the greens. Shoes designed for artificial turf or indoor soccer are the standard choice.

# What Is the American FootGolf League (AFGL)?

Published May 1, 2026· Updated July 18, 2026

If FootGolf has a "major league," this is it. The American FootGolf League (AFGL) is the national body that turns FootGolf from a fun round with friends into an organized competitive sport in the US.

## What the AFGL actually does

*   Affiliates and approves FootGolf courses that meet equipment and layout standards
*   Publishes a player Code of Conduct that governs tournament behavior
*   Runs a season-long tour of sanctioned events across affiliated clubs
*   Applies the international rule set maintained by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG)

## Why course affiliation matters

A course doesn't need AFGL affiliation to offer casual FootGolf: plenty of public courses run their own FootGolf layout for recreational play. Affiliation matters if you want to compete: only AFGL-affiliated courses can host sanctioned tour stops, and only rounds played under those rules count toward rankings and qualification for higher-level events.

## How to get involved competitively

1.   Play casually first to build consistency and confidence in your kicking technique
2.   Find your nearest AFGL-affiliated course and ask about local leagues or one-off tournaments
3.   Enter an amateur-level event before jumping into the full tour
4.   Track your scores to see how you'd stack up under tournament pressure

Not sure where to start looking? Our [course-finder guide](https://footgolfsport.com/find-footgolf-courses-near-me) walks through how to locate AFGL-affiliated courses in your area.

Wondering if top competitors can actually make a living at this? Read our honest look at [FootGolf prize money and player earnings](https://footgolfsport.com/blog/how-much-do-footgolf-players-make).

## Frequently asked questions

What is the American FootGolf League?The American FootGolf League (AFGL) is the official governing organization for competitive FootGolf in the United States. It approves and affiliates FootGolf courses, sets a player code of conduct, and runs an annual tour of sanctioned tournaments following the international rules set by the Federation for International FootGolf (FIFG).

## American FootGolf Federation

## The Governing Body of the Sport of FootGolf in the United States

## VISION

Our organization introduced FootGolf, "The Best Game Ever Invented", to the North American continent in 2011. For over a decade we have built the structure and promoted the sport across the United States and created the platform for the sport of FootGolf to be played competitively and socially.

![Image 6: AFGF_web_2025_to_play.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_2f14b0fa811443e2b8679fd4fa8f2129~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_490,h_280,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/AFGF_web_2025_to_play.png)

![Image 8: FIFG_web_2025_graphic_3.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_d1cb7b3fa4d6429383a63ce83f63afa1~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_148,h_122,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/FIFG_web_2025_graphic_3.png)

## OUR PILARS

FootGolf can be as fun or competitive as you want so you can invite your friends and family to the golf course with you. Soon you will discover the beauty of kicking a soccer ball on the fairways and FootGolf will become your favorite sport!

​

Learning to play FootGolf will improve your soccer skills.

[](https://www.usafootgolf.org/)

AFGF is the governing body and exclusive member in the United States of the Federation for International FootGolf.

American FootGolf Federation is a Non-Profit 501(c)3 organization that promotes and governs the sport of FootGolf across the country. Focused on Youth, Amateur and National FootGolf Teams the AFGF also provides golf course owners and operators with advice on FootGolf course design and equipment necessary to introduce the sport of FootGolf as a new activity in their facilities.

[PDF page 1]
FIFG COMPETITION RULES 2025

1.  OVERVIEW & MISSION STATEMENT

THE FIFG competitions and WORLD TOUR 2025 are based on an aspirational concept in
which every player is able to play and compete according to their possibilities, on a global
(World Ranking), regional (Regional Rankings) and national scale (National Rankings).

It’s mission is to foster friendship, camaraderie and competitiveness between all players
throughout the world by providing the platform for all Member Countries (MCs) to offer
different competitions.  The tournaments that MCs can offer will depend on their local
sports development measured by the amount of player memberships.

1.1 GENERAL GUIDELINES

The FIFG World Tour will be played entirely under the rules of the Federation for
International FootGolf.  Every tournament will follow the official rules of the sport, although
local rules may apply.  All local rules must be available for players before the start of each
tournament.

The FIFG Tournament Guidelines must be strictly followed by the MCs organizing the events.
Penalties will apply if rules are broken or not dealt with before a competition. We
understand that every country and/or region may be different therefore exceptions may
apply, though they need to be addressed prior to a tournament or before the calendar is
defined at the beginning of the year.

The World Tour encompasses two types of rankings: World Ranking and Regional Rankings.

1.2 CHANGES FOR 2025

●  MASTERS 1000 FIFG POINTS
●  WOMEN ABSOLUTE CATEGORY
●  LICENCE TYPES
●  TOURNAMENT CLASH UPDATES
●  TOURNAMENT STANDARDS
●  MANDATORY PACE OF PLAY REGULATION AND CONTROL
●  ANTI DOPING TESTING
●  REGISTRATION PROTOCOLS

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  1

[PDF page 2]
●  FIFG OFFICIAL’S ROLE AND AUTHORITY
●  ONLY PLAYERS FROM REGION CAN WIN REGIONAL TOUR PRIZE FUND OR WC/MS
QUALIFICATION

2.  REGIONS

Region 1: North, Central America & Caribbean Nations
NORTH AMERICAN TOUR

Region 2: South America
SOUTH AMERICAN TOUR

Region 3: Europe
EUROFOOTGOLF TOUR

Region 4: Asia & Oceania
ASIA-PACIFIC TOUR

Region 5: Africa
AFRICAN TOUR

3.  WORLD TOUR & REGIONAL TOURS

3.1 TOURNAMENT TYPES AND ALLOCATIONS

For the bidding process of the following year, the FIFG will consider the WT Licenses of the
Member Country up to October 31 of the current year.

FIFG WORLD MASTERS

The Masters is played during non-World Cup years.  It will be played during the 2025 season.
The World Masters has a qualification system where the best players from 2024 World &
Regional Rankings qualify to the events.  All regions are entitled to do a Regional Masters to
determine the qualified players of the Region.  Other players will be able to participate after
the confirmation of the qualified players.

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  2

[PDF page 3]
The World Masters will award 1000 FIFG points and will only count towards the World
Ranking.

FIFG MAJORS – FIFG 1000s

For future FIFG Majors and 500s MC’s must meet the minimum eligibility criteria to be able
to bid. This criteria will be available in a detailed document released Q1 2025. Please refer
to the FIFG bid process document

The FIFG Majors award 1000 FIFG points towards World and Regional Rankings.  There are a
total of 7 Majors in 2025, the distribution is as follows:

REGION 1  1
REGION 2  1
REGION 3  4
REGION 4  1
REGION 5  0

(Any MC selected to host a major and failing to host the tournament will not be eligible to
host a major for a minimum of 2 years. Appeals can be made to the FIFG in unforeseen
circumstances)

FIFG 500

REGIONS  AMOUNT
Region 1  3 – 4 *
Region 2  3 – 4 *
Region 3  10
Region 4  3 – 4*
Region 5  2-3 (200 min licenses)

*Flex in regions 1, 2 and 4 due to distances within countries.  Regions must present the
amount of FIFG 500s to FIFG for approval prior to the start of the season. Regions should
attempt to have a minimum of 3 500s in their region, to complete the minimum required for
World Ranking.

A MC that organizes a 1000 can’t host a 500, unless they have more than 12% of the total
World Tour Licenses based on previous year (440 WTL in 2025 for 2026).  Regional

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  3

[PDF page 4]
applications can also be made to the FIFG board to allow an MC to also host a 500.

Additional FIFG 500s can be approved by the Board on a suggestion by the Competitions
Committee, for special sponsored or promotional events.

FIFG 250

Every Member Country is allowed to organize an FIFG 250, even if awarded a FIFG 500 or
Major.  This allows MC to have their most important tournament to be minimum an FIFG
250.

If a Member county is not awarded with an FIFG 1000 or FIFG 500:
-  If 100 WT Licenses or more they can organize two FIFG 250s
-  If 150 WT Licenses or more they can organize three FIFG 250s.

Any member country that has an FIFG “Points per player” average of less than 9 points may
add additional FIFG 250s to bring the average above 9, however they must seek approval of
the Competitions Committee before doing so.

Regions should attempt to have a minimum of 4 250s in their region, to complete the
minimum required for World Ranking.

FIFG 250 events can be awarded to Member Countries with a significantly higher player per
tournament average number than other countries. These events will be awarded at the
discretion of the FIFG Competitions Committee.

FIFG 100

These tournaments are the entry level events for players into international tournaments.
Member Countries can flex up to a maximum of 14 100s, depending on the World Tour
Licenses.  A minimum also applies, since it is essential to introduce players into the
international spectrum (Regional & World).

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  4

[PDF page 5]
FLEX TABLE  MAX  MIN
Licenses  250+  14  10
200+  13  9
180+  12  8
150+  10  7
125+  9  6
100+  8  5
80+  7  4
50+  6  3
50-  5  1

NOTES:

FIFG Member Countries are NOT allowed to host FIFG ranking tournaments within multi
round FIFG tournaments. Example: A MC hosting a FIFG250 over 36 holes can’t host Round 1
FIFG 100 and/or FIFG 100 during Round 2. No exceptions.

If this occurs the MC will not be able to organize an FIFG 500, Major or Masters the
following year.

It is prohibited to host a local tournament on the same day and course together with an FIFG
500 or 1000 tournament, except for promotional tournaments that need to be approved by
the Competitions Committee. It is possible to do so for FIFG 100 or 250 events, however the
local tournament must have separate pairings and a recreational licence is recommended.

Holes played per day: FIFG MCs are allowed to stage more than 18 holes per day, maximum
36 holes.

3.2 WORLD RANKING

A global ranking encompassing FIFG tournaments in the different Regions based on points
scored over the last 12 months on a rolling basis counting the best results in:

FIFG Masters  1

FIFG 1000  2 (1 max. per region)

FIFG 500  3

FIFG 250  4
Total: Ten (10) FIFG competitions played with any region

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  5

[PDF page 6]
3.3 REGIONAL RANKINGS

A regional ranking encompassing tournaments of each region based on the best points
scored during the year:

Region 1  Region  2  Region 3  Region 4  Region 5
North America  South America  Europe  Asia & Oceania  Africa

FIFG 1000  1  1  1  1  -

FIFG 500  2  2  2  2  1

FIFG 250  3  3  3  3  3

FIFG 100  4  4  4  4  4

4.  FIFG COMPETITION REGULATIONS

4.1 CATEGORIES

Players will choose what category they want to represent at the moment they purchase
their World Tour License.

Men  All male players, excluding those in other categories
Senior Men (45+)  Male players born in 1979 and before.
Senior Plus (55+)  Male players born in 1969 and before.
Women  All female players, excluding juniors.
Women Senior (45+)  Female players born in 1979 and before
(ABSOLUTE CATEGORY FOR WOMEN/WOMEN SENIOR)
Juniors  All players born in 2007 and after.

Juniors are eligible to compete within the men or women classification if they have an
exemption authorized by the FIFG and FIFG Member Country.

4.2 FIFG PLAYER LICENSES

FIFG WORLD TOUR LICENCE

To play any FIFG competition, players must be affiliated to the FIFG Member in their country
of birth or permanent residency and hold a World Tour License.  A player must purchase a
WT Licence to be eligible to register for a FIFG tournament. A World Tour License of 20 euros

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  6

[PDF page 7]
(Junior licence 10 EUR) is required to play any tournament with FIFG ranking points.  A
player will be able to attend all FIFG events without any additional licenses or membership
fees other than from their MC.

A WT License is for a calendar year and is renewable in January of the new year regardless
of the month a player obtains it.  A player’s ranking will be activated after obtaining their
membership.

The basic requirement for a FIFG WTL is the MC membership. If a player has their MC
licence sanctioned or removed because of disciplinary reasons the WTL automatically
expires. The MC has to make the change in the official tournament software and report the
reason for the sanction within five days to the FIFG competitions committee and the rules
committee.

If a MC issues a WTL for a player that is not eligible as outlined in 4.5.1. there will be an
administration fine of 50 EUR per case.

Players from non-FIFG MCs must obtain their WT License directly through the FIFG.
(support@fifg.org).

RECREATIONAL LICENCE - NEW

The New Recreational Licence is an  initiative by FIFG to welcome new players into the world
of FootGolf. Designed specifically for amateur players and those curious to try the sport, this
licence offers an affordable and accessible way to experience FootGolf within an official
framework. The New Recreational Licence serves as an entry point for players who want to
explore FootGolf, providing a structured yet low-commitment way to participate. This
initiative aims to make FootGolf more inclusive, foster growth in participation, and inspire
players to join the global FootGolf community.

Key Features of the New Recreational Licence:

●  Introductory Access: Holders of the Recreational Licence can participate in one World
Tour (WT) 100 event, giving them a taste of competitive FootGolf in a friendly and
welcoming environment. The detailed conditions for this participation may vary
between Member Countries (MCs), ensuring local flexibility while maintaining a
consistent standard.

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  7

[PDF page 8]
●  Affordable Entry: Priced at just €2.50, this licence ensures that cost is not a barrier for
new players to experience the sport.
●  Seamless Upgrades: Players who wish to continue their FootGolf journey can easily
upgrade their Recreational Licence to the World Tour Licence. The €2.50 fee paid for the
Recreational Licence will be credited toward the cost of the World Tour Licence,
providing a seamless transition for those ready to commit to higher levels of
competition.
●  Free Registration in the Official Tournament Software System: Holders of the
Recreational Licence gain free registration in the FIFG's official tournament software
system (BlueGolf). This enables players to access event schedules, track their
participation, and gain insight into their performance, all through a professional and
easy-to-use platform.
●  Support for Member Countries: Member Countries are allowed to use the FIFG
tournament system (BlueGolf) at no additional cost for recreational purposes. The
Stableford tournament type is available free of charge, making it easier to organize local
events for recreational players.

Standards and Conduct:
To maintain the integrity of the sport, the FIFG and the MC reserves the right to deny a
Recreational Licence if a player’s behavior is found to be inconsistent with FIFG rules, the
World Tour document, or other regulations. This ensures a positive and fair environment
for all participants.

The New Recreational Licence is not just an entry ticket—it’s a stepping stone to
becoming a full-fledged member of the global FootGolf community. Whether you're a
curious beginner or looking to advance into the competitive realm with a World Tour
Licence, this licence provides an accessible and flexible starting point for your FootGolf
journey.

4.3 TOURNAMENT TYPES

In our effort to create a more cohesive FIFG community, we have developed a
comprehensive system for categorizing different tournaments globally. The key goal is to
establish a pyramid of competitive play that is accessible and beneficial to all Member
Countries (MC) and Players.

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  8

[PDF page 9]
T1  FIFG World Tour or FIFG Regional Tour Events: These events utilize the global
tournament system and are e  xclusively open to FIFG Members.
T2  FIFG Member Country Tournaments: This category includes National Tours or
tournaments integrated into a ranking system, and they are open to both FIFG Members
and members of FIFG Member countries.
T3  FIFG or FIFG Member Country Affiliated Tournaments: This includes tournaments held at
facilities recognized by Member Countries.
T4  Non FIFG Sanctioned Tournaments (NST): Non sanctioned tournaments hosted by
Member Countries or within  their borders.
T4.1  FIFG World Tour or Regional Tour events hosted by Member Countries,
allowing participation of non-FIFG Members.
T4.2  NST hosted by FIFG Members, permitting non-FIFG Member participation
(subject to non- approval by CC and Board).
T4.3  NST hosted by FIFG Members, not communicated or conflicting with
other FIFG tournaments.
T4.4  NST hosted by non-affiliated bodies.
T4.5  Tournaments organized or co-organized by a Member Country and a
non-approved competing tour.
T4.6  Tournaments organized by a Member Country with a tournament fee
exceeding 150 EUR or prize money exceeding 5,000 EUR without FIFG
points, unless pre-approved by CC or Board. Must not clash with FIFG
1000, 500.

PLAYER SANCTIONS/LIMITATIONS:

T4.1  No sanctions
T4.2  No sanctions; however, there may be restrictions imposed by the
Member Country.
T4.3  No sanctions; however, there may be restrictions imposed by the
Member Country.
T4.4  First tournament warning; the players lose the privilege of priority
registration,  a second tournament violation results in the player leaving
the FIFG tournament structure. Detailed procedures will be outlined in
the FIFG disciplinary documentation.

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  9

[PDF page 10]
FIFG MEMBER COUNTRY SANCTIONS:

T4.1  Investigation initiated with tournaments placed on hold; fees may be
applicable.
T4.2  Investigation initiated with tournaments placed on hold; fees may be
applicable.
T4.3  Removal of the opportunity to rank; fees may be applicable.
T4.4  No specific sanctions.
T4.5  Investigation initiated with a hold on all future MC tournaments and
suspension of the MC until the in  vestigation is completed.
If MC officials (board members, presidents, committee members rules
officials) play in this tournament it is considered as a MC supported
tournament and sanctions apply to the MC as if it had organised this
event.
T4.6  Investigation initiated with a hold on all future MC tournaments until the
investigation is completed.
All detailed sanctions  will be published in a new document that will
address all potential sanctions.

MC HOSTING TOURNAMENTS ABROAD:

MCs organizing tournaments in other countries must secure official approval from the
host country. The agreement must be submitted to the CC and the board at least one
board meeting before the event.

REVIEW PROCESS:

Any sanction is subject to FIFG Member Country dispute and is finalized by CC and the
FIFG Board.

BOARD MC RESTRICTIONS:

Member Country restrictions are supported by FIFG. Any restriction must be
communicated with FIFG  support@fifg.org.

4.4 TOURNAMENT GUIDELINES AND APPLICATIONS
FIFG Member countries can apply to host subject to guidelines and bid documents set by
the CC committee.

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  10

[PDF page 11]
4.4.1  TOURNAMENT HOSTING

MASTERS
The location of FIFG Masters will be decided by the FIFG Board, through a bidding process
by the CC.

MAJORS – FIFG 1000
The location of FIFG Majors will be through a bidding process by the CC, presented to the
FIFG Board. In smaller regions it can be recommended by each region and approved by the
FIFG Board.

FIFG 500
The location of FIFG 500 will be through a bidding process by the CC, presented to the FIFG
Board. In smaller regions it can be recommended by each region and approved by the FIFG
Board

FIFG 250
FIFG 250 allocated to all eligible FIFG MC. This level tournament must follow 3.1.

FIFG 100
FIFG 100 allocated to all eligible FIFG MC. This level tournament must follow 3.1.

4.4.2  REALLOCATION

MASTERS
In the event that a MC cannot fulfil the tournament, other MC or regions will be entitled to
submit a request to host to complete the annual allowance.

MAJORS
In the event that a MC or Region cannot fulfil their allocation, other MC or Regions will be
entitled to submit a request to host to complete the annual allowance.

OTHER TOURNAMENTS
FIFG 500-250-100 tournaments will be entitled to reallocate within each region and
according to the parameters set forth in 3.1.

4.4.3  TOURNAMENT CLASHES

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  11

[PDF page 12]
Masters / World Cup No clashes permitted

FIFG100  FIFG250  FIFG500  MAJOR
MASTERS  NO  NO  NO  NO
MAJOR  YES  OTHER REGION  NO  NO
FIFG 500  YES  YES  NO  NO
FIFG250  YES  YES  YES  OTHER REGION
FIFG100  YES  YES  YES  YES

No tournaments are allowed during the Masters dates that carry FIFG points or a prize
purse. Additionally no International competition can be held during these dates. Not
respecting this rule will result in a fine. In the case of other clashes laid out in the table
above a fine of 2 x of the FIFG points (FIFG 250 x 2 = 500 EUR) will apply.

In case an organizer moves for any reason to a high ranked (FIFG 250 or higher) tournament,
clashes should be avoided if possible.

4.4.4  TOURNAMENT STANDARDS

In order to standardize tournaments globally we generated the following information.  It is
not mandatory but strictly recommended in 2025* and valid 2026.
Event Sizing
Maximum Players:
●  1 Course: 180
●  2 Courses: 350
●  3 Courses: 500

These numbers can vary depending on daylight and weather conditions. Every organiser should
take into account also a back up time of at least two hours per day if a special weather situation
would appear.  More instructions will be described in the tournament guidelines and course
design standards.

In 2 course tournaments
●  Same categories play in the same course the same day.
○  Course 1: Men
○  Course 2: Female, Senior, Senior+, Female+, Junior
●  Cut Cup (Optional): Bottom 50% of players in each category after Day Two are eligible
for the "Cut Cup."

FIFG Competition Rules 2025  1.0  14.1.2025  12

[PDF page 13]
●  Cut Cup Rules:
○  Players compete in a separate Leaderboard within the Cut Cup.
○  Scores in the main competition remain valid; the Cut Cup is an additional
competitive opportunity.

Flights/Pairings
●  Categories must play together
○  Only exception during the first day of competition if wanted
●  Invert time during competition days:
○  If women play 9am day 1, they should play in the last flights in day 2. Example
below:
○  Day 1: Women, Senior, Men, Senior Plus
○  Day 2: Senior Plus, Men, Senior Women
○  The largest category should always be in the middle because it is when the
climate is similar.  For example if Men play at 8:00, some players will play with a
wet surface for the first hour and other players will start with a dry surface.

Flight/Pairing Draw
●  Option 1: By current world ranking
●  Option 2: Random Draw - placing top ranked players in a similar time zone.

Scorecard
●  Each player should receive a scorecard and exchange them at the first hole, in order to
identify who is each player’s marker.
●  It is the players’ responsibility to verify their scorecards at the end of the round and sign
it.

## By joining the U.S. FootGolf Tour (USFGT) you are on your way to playing "The Best Game Ever Invented". Take the steps to compete alongside your friends and peers to see where you rank against like players from all over the country. You will be joining other players of the sport for a fun and competitive round of FootGolf.  
  
 Under the official umbrella of the American FootGolf Federation you can be confident that as an amateur player you are learning to play the game right. Make sure to review Rules of Play, Dress Code, Tournament Formats, Players Categories and Ranking Points.Take the time to review the rules and guidelines to get confident with playing the sport.

* USFGT Players Licenses are valid for 12 months from teh day of purchase. By proceeding, you agree to and accept the USFGT terms of use and privacy policy. Buying a membership for someone else.For questions about the USFGT Players License please call us 760-501-0100 or email us at [usa@footgolf.net](mailto:usa@footgolf.net)

## USFGT PLAYER

## LICENSE BENEFITS

​

*   ​Lifetime Member Number​

*   USFGT Official Ball Marker

*   Member profile page

*   Official FootGolf Tee

*   Downloadable Tour Card

*   Earn points to qualify for major events

*   Player Ranking

*   Player Index/Rating (NEW!) *

*   Access to event results, stats and rankings

*   Tour updates and sporting e-news letter

*   Member discounts on official merchandise at the FootGolf Store

*   FREE iPhone and Android App

​

Tournament Discounts

When you register to compete in the USFGT sanctioned events, you will be able to compete for a $5 discount as compared to non-members. Play a couple of sanctioned events each year and your membership essentially pays for itself.

​

Track Improvement

Your USFGT player profile page will be updated with your tour points every time you compete in a sanctioned event, which updates your player ranking and index/rating. It shows you how you compare to others in the sport. Compete more, improve your ranking, index/rating and watch your player points add up for qualifications in USFGT Major Events.

​

Grow the sport

A portion of your USFGT membership helps the organization fund valuable initiatives that grow our sport at the grassroots level and helps to elevate it to the mainstream.

​

As a license player of the U.S. Amateur FootGolf Tour, you will join a group of people who are not only passionate about the sport but also see several benefits from their annual membership. Play, compete and help grow the sport of FootGolf!

AFGL TOUR l FOOTGOLF MAJOR LEAGUE

The [AFGL TOUR](https://www.footgolfusa.com/afgltour)is the top classification for the sport of FootGolf in the United States. All members of the U.S. National FootGolf Team (Team USA) must have the[AFGL TOUR license](https://www.footgolfusa.com/players).

The tournaments on this tour are played by[AFGL TOUR licensed players](https://www.footgolfusa.com/roster) exclusively, on AFGL Certified Courses, and under the umbrellas of the American FootGolf Federation, North American FootGolf Confederation and Federation for International FootGolf.

​

For more information visit all the pages related to the tour in this website, contact us by telephone at +1 (760) 501-0100 Ext. 106, or by email at [usa@footgolf.net](mailto:usa@footgolf.net) | Thank you!

​

![Image 35: AFGL_web_2023_AFGL_tour_back_R1.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_aa07748b2cc643a1aa03073715f970c2~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_409,h_868,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/ef005a_aa07748b2cc643a1aa03073715f970c2~mv2.png)

The AFGL Tour is comprised of all ranking-point tournaments managed by the AFGL.

​

The North American Tour will be played in Mexico, Canada, Honduras and United States. It is comprised of all ranking-point tournaments managed by the FIFG Members Countries.

​

The World Tour is comprised of all ranking-point tournaments managed by the FIFG.

​

The Tours have been designed for FIFG Member Countries and Affiliated Players and are played on Accredited FootGolf Courses that have been reviewed to be a part of the competitions.

Ranking points for ALL TOURS under the FIFG umbrella start from zero on Jan 1st.​

![Image 36: AFGL_web_2023_AFGL_tour_back_WT.png](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/ef005a_8266f7fadc8a420c975eb2ad2804dbb5~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_410,h_868,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/ef005a_8266f7fadc8a420c975eb2ad2804dbb5~mv2.png)

Men 18 and over,Senior Men 46 and older,Senior Men Plus 56 and older,Women 18 and older,Women 46 and older and FootGolf Clubs in the AFGL First Division.Juniors under 18 years old can participate in the Men 18-45, or Women 18-45 categories with an exemption.Ranking Points are valid for the AFGL Tour, FIFG North American Tour, and FIFG World Tour.

Memberships renew on an annually based on the calendar year so may need to be renewed midseason of the AFGL tour.

## National Congress of State Games

## About the State Games of America

**What is it and who can participate?**

The State Games of America is an Olympic-style event featuring competition between State Games medal winners (gold, silver, bronze) from across the nation. There are currently 30 states conducting or organizing statewide sports festivals known as State Games.

**When is the event held?**

The event is hosted every two years on the even year (i.e. 2022, 2024, 2026…).

**Where is the event held?**

The 2026**[State Games of America](http://stategamesofamerica.com/)** will be held in State College, PA.

## From today's featured article

[![Image 4: White-headed fruit dove](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/PtilopusEugeniaeKeulemans_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-PtilopusEugeniaeKeulemans_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PtilopusEugeniaeKeulemans_(cropped).jpg "White-headed fruit dove")

The **[white-headed fruit dove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-headed_fruit_dove "White-headed fruit dove")** (_Ptilinopus eugeniae_) is a species of bird in the pigeon family, [Columbidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbidae "Columbidae"). It was [described](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species_description "Species description") by [John Gould](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Gould "John Gould") in 1856, and the [specific name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Specific_name_(zoology) "Specific name (zoology)")_eugeniae_ honours [Eugénie de Montijo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eug%C3%A9nie_de_Montijo "Eugénie de Montijo"). Adults of the species have white heads, a purplish-red breast patch, a grey shoulder patch, olive-green [upperparts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_bird_terms#upperparts "Glossary of bird terms"), greenish [underparts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_bird_terms#underparts "Glossary of bird terms") with a blue tinge, and a yellowish [vent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_bird_terms#vent "Glossary of bird terms"). Juveniles have green heads with the white restricted to the forehead and upper throat, a much smaller grey shoulder patch, and the red breast patch restricted to the centre of the breast. The species is [endemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endemism "Endemism") to [Makira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makira "Makira") and the nearby islands of [Ugi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ugi_Island "Ugi Island") and [Malaupaina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaupaina "Malaupaina") in the Solomon Islands. It inhabits lowland, hill, and ridge forest, along with neighbouring agricultural areas, and is especially common in [foothills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foothills "Foothills"). Its diet consists of small-seeded fruits and berries. The [IUCN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Union_for_Conservation_of_Nature "International Union for Conservation of Nature") considers it a [least-concern species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Least-concern_species "Least-concern species"). Although it can adapt to [disturbed habitat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disturbance_(ecology) "Disturbance (ecology)"), it is threatened by [deforestation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deforestation "Deforestation") and [habitat loss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habitat_destruction "Habitat destruction"). _(**[Full article...](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-headed\_fruit\_dove "White-headed fruit dove")**)_

## Did you know...

[![Image 5: Main building of the Marin County Civic Center](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/Marin_County_Civic_Center_-_35.jpg/250px-Marin_County_Civic_Center_-_35.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Marin_County_Civic_Center_-_35.jpg "Main building of the Marin County Civic Center")

Main building of the Marin County Civic Center

*   ... that **[a California county government building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marin_County_Civic_Center "Marin County Civic Center")**_(pictured)_ inspired elements of Naboo in the _Star Wars_ prequel trilogy?
*   ... that **[Toribia Álvaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toribia_%C3%81lvaro "Toribia Álvaro")** became a candidate for the Bolivian parliament because no other women of the [Uru of Lake Poopó](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uru-Murato "Uru-Murato") were willing to run?
*   ... that [Mark Twain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Twain "Mark Twain") said that the **[Charlton Public Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlton_Public_Library_(Massachusetts) "Charlton Public Library (Massachusetts)")** banning one of his books was "not of the slightest interest to him"?
*   ... that Dutch painter **[Henry van Velthuysen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_van_Velthuysen "Henry van Velthuysen")** dismissed a contemporary's works as "infantile construction-kit shapes"?
*   ... that the spirit **[Ti Jean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ti_Jean "Ti Jean")**, a one-legged cannibal highwayman, evokes colonial fear of [maroons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maroons "Maroons")?
*   ... that abolitionist **[Alba Honeywell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alba_Honeywell "Alba Honeywell")** said he sold the first published copy of anti-slavery novel _[Uncle Tom's Cabin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle\_Tom's\_Cabin "Uncle Tom's Cabin")_?
*   ... that **[Samoa has 225 species of fern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flora_of_Samoa "Flora of Samoa")**, more than New Zealand, a country 85 times larger?
*   ... that **[Kelvin Kong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelvin_Kong "Kelvin Kong")**, the first recognised Indigenous Australian surgeon, was made a member of the Order of Australia for his services to Indigenous health?
*   ... that **[Pan Pan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan_Pan_(giant_panda) "Pan Pan (giant panda)")** is thought to have had more than 130 descendants?

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

Sport combining the gameplay of golf and football

**Codeball** is an individual sport combining the gameplay of [golf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golf "Golf") and [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football").

## Rules

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Codeball&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Rules")]

Codeball is played on a fairway consisting of usually 14 bowls, similar to the holes in golf. A six-inch rubber ball is kicked from a marked kickoff area, and once the ball comes to rest, it is kicked again. The process is repeated until the ball is sunk into the bowl. The goal of codeball is to reach the bowl using as few kicks as possible.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Codeball&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

Codeball was invented in 1929 by a Chicago doctor named William Edward Code, who developed the game for his friend. At the time, Code's friend sought an inexpensive outdoor game suited to large playgrounds.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codeball#cite_note-1) Almost forgotten today, the game reached its peak of popularity in the 1930s. By summer 1932, at least 12 codeball courses were in existence, chiefly in the upper Midwest.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codeball#cite_note-Golfdom_32-2)

It was officially sanctioned by the [Amateur Athletic Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_Athletic_Union "Amateur Athletic Union") in 1929.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codeball#cite_note-Golfdom_32-2)

The first codeball championship was won by Bert Gates, with a score of 69 for 15 bowls, at [Forest Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forest_Park_(St._Louis) "Forest Park (St. Louis)"), [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis"), in 1935.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codeball#cite_note-3)

## Variations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Codeball&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Variations")]

Code invented later on codeball-on the-court, a combination of [American handball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_handball "American handball") and association football. It is a two-person sport played with a six-inch ball on a playing court. The ball is kicked against a wall, and the opposing player must return the ball on the second bounce. The original sport is sometimes called Codeball-on-the-Green to distinguish it from the newer game. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## about us

![Image 12: A group of people cheering next to a Mickey Mouse mascot.](https://www.footgolf.sport/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Rectangle-36.jpg)

The Federation for International FootGolf’s main function is to promote worldwide recognition of the sport of FootGolf. It oversees the international development and growth to ensure equitable play for all players worldwide.  
  
Establishing a new sport in the world is not an easy task. Before its launch, members of the FIFG around the world had been working tirelessly to introduce, establish and promote the sport at grassroots level.  
  
It was very clear from the beginning that a structure needed to be created in order for the sport to be played at all levels.To reach this goal, the FIFG established the international rules of play and constitution of FootGolf under which all members agree to abide.  
  
The FIFG recognizes only one member per country. Countries currently not represented by a member may submit a request for the process and terms to become a member.

## The game of  
FootGolf

FootGolf is played from the teeing zone with each player aiming for the hole on the green zone in the fewest number of kicks. It is played with minimal supervision of a marshal and depends on the integrity of the player to show consideration for other players and to abide by the rules.  
  
All footgolfers should conduct themselves in a disciplined manner demonstrating courtesy at all times and sportsmanship regardless of how competitive they may be.   
  
This is the spirit of FootGolf.

## Get Started  
with FootGolf

[Step 1. Learn the Basics](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

To play FootGolf, you’ll need a standard size 5 soccer ball, comfortable sportswear, and the official attire: knee-high socks, a collared shirt, and golf-style shorts. Proper footwear – like turf shoes or indoor soccer shoes – is also essential, as cleats are not allowed.

Having the right gear ensures you’re ready to play in comfort and style!

FootGolf combines the precision of golf with the kicking skills of soccer. The objective is to kick a standard size 5 soccer ball into a series of 21-inch diameter cups in as few shots as possible.

Familiarize yourself with the FootGolf Rule Book and become a pro on the course!

[Step 2. Find a Course](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

FootGolf is played on specially designed courses or modified golf courses with designated FootGolf holes. With courses available worldwide, you can easily find one near you to start playing.

[Step 3. Get the Right Equipment](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

To play FootGolf, you’ll need a standard size 5 soccer ball, comfortable sportswear, and the official attire: knee-high socks, a collared shirt, and golf-style shorts. Proper footwear – like turf shoes or indoor soccer shoes – is also essential, as cleats are not allowed.  
Having the right gear ensures you’re ready to play in comfort and style!

[Step 4. Join a Club or Organization](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

Becoming part of a FootGolf club or national organization connects you with other players, helps you improve your game, and gives you access to exclusive events and competitions.

[Step 5. Practice and Play](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

Like any sport, FootGolf requires practice to develop skill and strategy. Focus on improving your precision, shot power, and course management.  
Start by playing casual rounds with friends or training on different terrains to enhance your technique!

[Step 6. Participate in Events](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

FootGolf offers tournaments for all skill levels, from local competitions to international championships. Competing is a great way to challenge yourself and experience the excitement of the sport.

[Step 7. Player Benefits of FootGolf](https://footgolf.sport/champions/)

##### Accessibility:

FootGolf is easier to learn and play compared to traditional golf, making it accessible to a wider range of people.

##### Cost-Effective:

The equipment required for FootGolf is minimal, which makes it a more affordable sport.

##### Physical Activity:

It provides a good form of exercise, combining the skills of soccer with the strategic play of golf.

##### Social Interaction:

FootGolf encourages social interaction and can be played in groups, fostering a sense of community.

##### International Opportunities:

Players affiliated with FIFG members can qualify to represent their country in international tournaments.

[Join Footgolf](https://footgolf.sport/champions/#join-footgolf-popup)

Keep up with the latest news, rule changes, and events by following official FIFG channels. Stay connected through our official FIFG website and our social media pages
